name: Northern Leaf Blight
description: A fungal disease that causes long elliptical gray-green or tan lesions on maize leaves. Lesions develop in cool, humid conditions.
symptoms: Long elliptical gray-green lesions on leaves
Lesions turning tan with dark borders as they mature
Lesions appearing first on lower leaves
Premature leaf death in severe infections
Reduced grain fill due to reduced photosynthetic area
causes: Fungal spores overwintering in crop residue
treatments: Apply fungicides containing azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin at first sign of disease
Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at 7-14 day intervals during humid conditions
Use systemic fungicides for active infections
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant maize varieties
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation
Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening
